advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Either reject or warn on `--dry-run` without `--repair`, matching the documented 'with --repair' contract.
evidence: link_audit.py:271-272 accepts `--dry-run` as a known arg unconditionally

help/link-audit.txt: `--dry-run   with --repair, preview without writing any event`
advisory.finding: `--dry-run` passed WITHOUT `--repair` is silently accepted and behaves identically to a plain scan (it is only consulted via `do_repair and not dry_run`), contradicting the help/docs which state `--dry-run   with --repair, preview without writing`. scenarios: `rebar link-audit --dry-run` (no --repair) runs a plain scan with no warning that --dry-run had no effect.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that patches _reconciler_in_flight to True and asserts run_repair raises CommandError and writes nothing.
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/link_audit.py:227 `if _reconciler_in_flight(repo_root):` then `raise CommandError(...)`
docs/ticket-model.md:162 '`--repair` takes the write lock, refuses to run while a reconciler pass is in flight'

ABSENCE: search_files for `_reconciler_in_flight` shows uses only in link_audit.py/fsck_repair.py source; test_link_audit.py never patches it to True nor calls run_repair, so the guard path is unexercised.
advisory.finding: run_repair's reconciler-in-flight guard (raises CommandError, refusing to repair while a reconciler pass is in flight) has no test. This is documented as a core safety property ('refuses to run while a reconciler pass is in flight'), but no test injects _reconciler_in_flight() -> True, so a regression removing or inverting the guard would let --repair write under a live reconciler undetected.
scenarios: A refactor drops or inverts the in-flight check
run_repair proceeds while a reconciler pass holds the lock, corrupting convergence
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a test monkeypatching link_audit._reconciler_in_flight -> True over a store with findings, asserting run_repair raises CommandError and the event count is unchanged.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add tests injecting a CyclicDependencyError and a CommandError (and an add_dependency failure at the link-first step) and assert the finding is marked unrepairable with no dependency lost.
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/link_audit.py:55-60 comment: 'catching ValueError alone would let a real write failure escape and abort the run mid-repair'
tests/scripts/graph/test_link_audit.py:195-196 the only injected fault is `raise ValueError("unlink exploded")`; test_repair_is_resumable also injects ValueError only
ABSENCE: no test injects CyclicDependencyError or CommandError, and no test injects a failure at the add_dependency (link-first) step for a mis-escalated finding.
advisory.finding: The repair fault-catch breadth (_REPAIR_FAULTS = ValueError, CyclicDependencyError, CommandError) is asserted only for ValueError. The module's own comment argues catching ValueError alone is a bug because CyclicDependencyError/CommandError derive from Exception, but no test injects a CyclicDependencyError or CommandError (nor a failure at the link-first add_dependency step), so narrowing the catch back to (ValueError,) would pass the entire suite — the very regression the code guards against is untested.
scenarios: add_dependency raises CyclicDependencyError during a mis-escalated repair
advisory.suggested_fix: Parametrize the fault-injection test over ValueError, CyclicDependencyError, and CommandError at both _unlink_edge and add_dependency seams, asserting repair_status == 'unrepairable' and both edges survive.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the canonicalized deps[] target_id used for enumeration with the raw-form target_id matched by `_get_link_info`/`_write_unlink` so alias-form legacy links can be unlinked.
evidence: link_audit.py:77-79 enumerates edges from `dep.get('target_id')` — the reducer's compiled deps[]
_processors.py:392-394 `canonical = resolve_ticket_id(raw_target, tracker_dir); if canonical: resolved_target = canonical` — deps[] target is the CANONICAL uuid
unlink.py:74 `if tid == target_id:` matches the RAW event `data.get('target_id', data.get('target',''))` (unlink.py:64), never re-resolved to canonical
repair_finding compares `would_cancel != finding['relation']` and declines with reason 'ambiguous-pair: unlink would cancel ...nothing' (link_audit.py:178-185)
dropped.finding: `_blocking_edges` reads `dep['target_id']` from the reducer's deps[], which `process_link` canonicalizes from alias/short-hex to the ticket UUID, but repair's `_unlink_would_cancel`/`_write_unlink` match against the RAW on-disk LINK event's `data.target_id`. For a legacy link whose event stored the target in alias/short-hex form — exactly the 'written under an older rule' population this tool targets — `_get_link_info` finds no match, so repair falsely declines the edge as `ambiguous-pair: unlink would cancel 'nothing'` and never fixes it.
scenarios: A legacy blocking LINK whose event stored the target as an alias/short-hex id (not the canonical uuid) is classified fine by resolve_hierarchy_link but cannot be matched by the unlink resolution, so --repair leaves it outstanding forever.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the code comment/plan wording so the ambiguous-pair guard's relation-match semantics (vs. the plan's 'count != 1') are explicit.
evidence: ticket plan: 'the driver counts the pair's net-active links; when that count is not exactly 1 the finding is reported unrepairable with reason ambiguous-pair'
implementation compares relation identity instead: `would_cancel = _unlink_would_cancel(...); if would_cancel != finding['relation']:` (link_audit.py:178-179)
`_get_link_info` returns the single most-recent net-active link for the pair (unlink.py:74-78), not a count
dropped.finding: The ambiguous-pair guard diverges from the plan's stated safety design: the plan specifies counting the pair's net-active links and declining when the count is not exactly 1, but the implementation instead compares only the most-recent link's relation (`_unlink_would_cancel != finding['relation']`). These differ when a pair holds two same-relation links or a blocking edge that is the newest of several relations; the implemented check is what unlink actually cancels (so it is safe), but the divergence from the documented count-based rule is undocumented in the code and could mislead future maintainers.
scenarios: A maintainer reading the plan expects a count-of-1 invariant but finds a relation-equality check; the two disagree on a pair carrying two same-relation net-active links.
